title: Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection is hampered by conflicting distributional assumptions, poor scalability, and difficulty covering global, local, and dependency anomalies. ISER partitions space with hyperspheres whose radii are a monotonic transform of local density, builds a t-dimensional ensemble representation Φ(x), and scores points by averaging (ISER-A) or cosine similarity to an all-ones anomaly reference (ISER-S), and can also feed Φ into a sign-inverted Isolation Forest (ISER-IF). On 20 real-world datasets ISER-S attains the best average AUC-ROC of 0.8523, and ISER-IF improves over iForest on all nine reported datasets (e.g., Ionosphere 0.8530 to 0.9314).

match_target.why: User-specified target. Ionosphere is tiny (351x32), so reproducing ISER-IF is cheap, and it directly demonstrates the paper's key extension that the ISER ensemble representation Φ, when fed to a sign-inverted Isolation Forest, fixes iForest's axis-parallel/local-anomaly failures (0.8530 to 0.9314).

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUC-ROC is a bounded score printed in [0,1] (0.9314) on Ionosphere, a small set (351 < 2,000 examples); the paper reports no std over the 5 repeats, so the band is 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: For each of t partitionings, sample ψ points from D without replacement; every sampled point z becomes a hypersphere center whose radius is the distance to its nearest neighbor within the sampled subset.
requirements.quote: The radius of this hypersphere is determined by the distance between z and its nearest neighbor in Di \ {z}

requirements.stmt: For a query x, the covering set is Ci(x)={z in Di : ||x−z|| ≤ r[z]}, and the representing center is the covering hypersphere of smallest radius.
requirements.quote: we select the covering hypersphere with the smallest radius

requirements.stmt: Per-partition value is φi(x)=1−1/r[ẑi(x)] when x is covered, and φi(x)=1 when no hypersphere in Hi covers x.
requirements.quote: When x is covered by no hypersphere in Hi, we assign φi(x) = 1

requirements.stmt: The ensemble representation is the concatenation Φ(x)=[φ1(x),...,φt(x)] in R^t.
requirements.quote: The ensemble representation of point x is constructed by concatenating the coverage indicators from all t partitionings

requirements.stmt: Average-based score ISER-A is the arithmetic mean of the t representation components.
requirements.quote: The average-based anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean of all ensemble components

requirements.stmt: Similarity-based score ISER-S is the cosine similarity between Φ(x) and the all-ones anomaly reference vector 1=[1,...,1].
requirements.quote: The similarity-based anomaly score is computed using cosine similarity between the point's ensemble representation and the anomaly reference vector

requirements.stmt: ISER-IF applies Isolation Forest to Φ(x) and inverts the score so longer average path length means more anomalous: S_ISER-IF(x,n)=1−2^(−E(h(Φ(x)))/c(n)).
requirements.quote: This modification ensures that shorter path lengths in the ISER feature space correspond to lower anomaly scores

requirements.stmt: Hyperparameters: sample size ψ searched over {2m, m=1,2,...,8} (i.e., 2,4,...,16) with default number of partitionings t=200.
requirements.quote: ψ ∈{2m, m = 1, 2, . . . , 8} and with default t = 200

requirements.stmt: Evaluation metric is AUC-ROC; each experiment is repeated 5 times and the average is reported.
requirements.quote: Each experiment is repeated 5 times and reported average results

requirements.stmt: Unsupervised, contaminated setting: the whole dataset (normal + anomalous) is available during training; no clean normal-only training set is assumed.
requirements.quote: our experiments assume access to the entire dataset containing both normal and anomalous instances during training

requirements.stmt: For ISER-IF, run iForest on the transformed feature space Φ(x) rather than on the original input space.
requirements.quote: By applying iForest to this transformed feature space rather than the original data space

requirements.stmt: Use the 20 real-world benchmark datasets from PyOD and ODDS with the statistics listed in Table II.
requirements.quote: We conduct experiments on 20 real-world benchmark datasets from PyOD [32] and ODDS [33] repositories

data.name: 20 tabular anomaly-detection datasets: Annthyroid, backdoor, breastw, celeba, fault, glass, Ionosphere, Landsat, Lymphography, mnist, musk, pendigits, Pima, satellite, satimage-2, shuttle, skin, speech, vowels, WPBC (statistics in Table II)
data.how_to_get: From the PyOD [32] toolbox dataset loaders and the ODDS [33] library (https://shebuti.com/outlier-detection-datasets-odds); sizes/anomaly counts are listed in Table II of the paper.
